summary: Changed the landing page CTA from a passive "Learn more" link to `/step1` to a direct "무료 회원가입" (Free sign-up) button pointing to `/email`, skipping two intermediate funnel steps and reducing time-to-action from 6 steps to effectively 3 — because shortening the path to email capture is the single most reliable lever for increasing funnel completion rates.

Removed the "intro" and "details" pre-email steps from the funnel, cutting the path from 6 steps to 4, because every extra step before users provide their email is a drop-off point and eliminating this friction directly increases the fraction who reach signup completion.

Replaced the generic welcome page with a benefit-driven headline, three concrete value bullets, and a styled CTA button that says "무료로 가입하기 →" (Sign up free →) instead of the weak "자세히 알아보기" (Learn more), because a clear value proposition with a strong action-oriented CTA directly reduces the mental barrier to clicking and entering the funnel.

Changed the CTA from an unstyled "Learn more" text link to a prominent blue button reading "무료로 시작하기" (Start for free), replaced the friction-inducing "slowly read before proceeding" copy with a direct benefit statement, and added an action-oriented headline — because a visually distinct, benefit-framed CTA button directly reduces the hesitation barrier at the point of conversion.

Changed the landing page CTA from the passive "자세히 알아보기" (Learn more) to a visually prominent button with "지금 무료로 시작하기" (Start free now) plus "무료" (free) and "30초" (30 seconds) messaging, because a clear, benefit-driven CTA with a visual affordance is the single highest-impact lever for reducing bounce and driving users into the funnel.

Replaced the passive "learn more" landing page with a benefit-driven headline, a prominent blue CTA button labeled "무료 회원가입" (Free Sign Up), and social proof — eliminating all friction-inducing language that told users to "slowly read before proceeding," which was suppressing click-through to the funnel.
